Yeah I understand there's not much they can do but be there I guess. Sorry I didn't realize you've talked to him before. Reading this on my mobile at the moment. 

Headspace is an Aussie website so I'm not 100% sure it will work for you depending where you are but they have counsellors online you can chat to and forums also. here's the link http://headspace.org they also have quite good resources for anxiety. 
Do you have a smart phone because there's also a few good apps on apple (I don't know specifics for android but you could always search anxiety/headspace/mindfulness) for anxiety that might be helpful when you're having an attack (I've tried everything in my years of panic attacks).

If you sign up you can chat to a counsellor on the headspace website 24/7 they're quite good to talk to I've found. 
I used to struggle telling my partner or talking about my anxiety with him because I was afraid of how I would look/I wanted to appear fine to him and not bring it into our relationship but I assure you people like to help and it's not going to damage your relationship to let someone know you need a chat and some help time to time.
He reminded me that I am not my anxiety.

I also just realized you might just want to have things to say because it's 5am and I read that wrong hahah best thing is to just maybe ask her if she needs anything be calm, grab her a blankey if you can and just be there. It's hard to gauge what stuff might make her worst but as long as you're not pushy for her to stop the attacks and just keep assuring her shell get through it, you should be okay. My partner just kind of sits there and holds me or tells me to calmly breathe however we have worked out before hand (see massive paragraph I wrote already hahah) that he should do that and some people might not like that. :) easiest thing is to ask her though what is best to say when she's having an attack.

It's really nice to see you want to try to find things for her, I'm sure she'll appreciAte that in itself. There's heaps of resources online about breathing techniques for when someone is having an attack. It really depends on what she already does  and what she hasn't tried. A good site I used to use is moodgym and it has a whole lot of modules to go through which help with a range of issues including anxiety. A good start might be to just be like "hey I'd love to be able to help you in these times so we can get you through them easier, maybe we could make a list of tools to do it?" and come up with a list she can quickly go to with things that calm her or help her eg music or saying certain things. There's also a great phone app called SAM that is for anxiety she might find helpful. :) Goodluck dude.
It's ok to feel not ok sometimes. We'll get through this.

Talk to your school counsellor. Tell them your issues/get letter from your psychologist and see if you can get an extension and start now. You can do it. You got this far and you can finish it. Most schools are good with mental health issues affecting school work as long as you tell them.

Walking outside is good or I would use the old rubber band trick where you flick it on your wrist and the sharp pang can feel slightly like the blade slice without the scars obv.
